newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds soft at close, more selling seen.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds soft at close, more selling seen.

text.p: Argentine bonds pared losses in late trading Monday but dealers said the tone was soft and the market may be heading for stronger selling.

"The market fell in the afternoon and is trying to recover now towards the close, but there's an undercurrent of selling," one dealer said. "It looks to me like this may be the onset of a spell of profit-taking, which should be unleashed within the next 10 sessions."
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 shed 3/8 to 94-3/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 tumbled $5.06 to 121.60.
Traders said the drop was linked to volatility on the U.S. and the Argentine stock markets, and they remained bullish medium-term.
Argentina's blue-chip MerVal index fell 1.7 percent Monday on currency jitters in Brazil, dealers said.
"Nothing here really has changed. It's just that at these prices bonds aren't strong enough to keep pushing higher. They need to pause or else fresh incentives," another trader said.
